implication: Regulation 31(4)–(5) disclosures indicate a substantial acquisition (≥25% threshold) or open offer commencement; this filing establishes public notice and marks the formal entry into SEBI takeover protocol, with downstream requirements for creeping acquisition limits, open offer conduct and post-acquisition shareholding caps.

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 - Regulation 31(4) & 31(5)
framework.note: central - Mandatory disclosure when acquirer crosses 25% shareholding or announces open offer; prescribes form, timing (within 2 business days), and content (acquirer, target, offer price, etc.); cornerstone of takeover transparency.

central - Defines 'acquisition' (shares + voting rights ≥25%) and exemptions (inheritance, inter-se transfers, rights issues); establishes creeping threshold (9.99% per financial year without triggering open offer if <25%).

central - Mandatory open offer at highest price paid in prior 52 weeks (or average if higher); applies to acquirer crossing 25%; prescribes offer period (4–10 weeks), public announcement, and consideration format (cash/securities).
central - Lock-in: acquirer and associates restricted from selling ≥5% acquired shares for 6 months post-open offer close; exemptions for inter-se transfers and stock pledges.

amended - Exempt acquisitions (statutory authority, inter-se transfer, inheritance); amended 2018 to clarify preferential allotment trigger and 2022 for e-auction extensions; review current carve-outs.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 - Regulation 30 & 31
framework.note: central - Continuous disclosure and material event reporting; Reg. 31 requires listed company to inform stock exchanges of acquisition and takeover within 24 hours of public announcement.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013 - Section 149 & 150 (Director appointment) and Schedule XIII (Related party)
framework.note: procedural - If post-acquisition shareholding triggers director board composition change (proportionality rule) or related-party arm's-length review, Companies Act thresholds apply.
procedural - Post-acquisition shareholding restrictions: acquirer cannot hold >75% without delisting; delisting framework applies if >90%.

headline: Fusion Finance Limited: Disclosure under SEBI Takeover Regulations (Regulation 31(4) & 31(5))
sum: Fusion Finance Limited submitted a mandatory disclosure under SEBI's Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers (SAST) Regulations 2011, specifically Regulation 31(4) and 31(5), to the NSE, signalling a notifiable acquisition event or open offer trigger.
detail: Fusion Finance Limited filed a Regulation 31(4)–(5) disclosure with the NSE, which is triggered when an acquirer crosses 25% shareholding or announces an open offer. The disclosure is a cornerstone of the SEBI SAST Regulations 2011 framework, mandating public disclosure of acquisition intent, acquirer identity, offer price (if applicable), and target shareholding. This filing does not itself reveal the acquirer, offer value or target stake, but establishes the regulatory checkpoint at which the takeover process enters transparent, supervised territory. The company's submission to the exchange creates a public record and triggers the mandatory open offer and post-acquisition lock-in regime.
